test.name: Create a stub person when the will names a son with no tree match
test.description: The full-text will of Thomas Flynn names two sons. Patrick is already in the tree (I1); the will also names 'my son James Flynn' (assertion a_005, role heir_2). There is NO James Flynn in tree.gedcomx.json (only Patrick I1, Thomas I2, Mary I3), so the persona matches no existing person. Per agents/person-evidence.md Step 5 and research-schema-spec.md §8 (line 656 — 'Person stubs may be created by person-evidence when a newly discovered person doesn't yet exist'), person-evidence must mint a new person for James — via materialize_facts create-or-enrich, so he arrives carrying the will's SOURCED name fact (a_005, ref resolved to tree S-entry S4) rather than a name-only shell — and link a_005 to the new person. (This test isolates the fact-carrying mint + link; edge-writing is graded by the 'Person minting and connecting edges' dimension, exercised by the household-skeleton fixture.) This is the headline gap: stub creation is instructed and spec-authorized but was never exercised (the harness TREE_OWNERSHIP_TABLE omitted person-evidence from the persons AND relationships writers, so a correct fact-carrying-mint + edge run failed the universal ownership validator until this PR's fix, which grants person-evidence both).
test.xfail_reason: Owned by issue #2943 (a record-derived person with no source reference is the provenance gap that lets circular corroboration through). The skill sometimes mints James via tree_edit add_person instead of materialize_facts, which creates him with no source ref and fails test_stub_person_created_and_linked; the per-test context requires the persona form with a sourced name (a_005 -> src_004 -> S4). That route is also the one place research_append's circular-corroboration walk cannot see, because the walk needs a source ref; 274 of 711 run-added corpus persons are ref-less. Measured 2026-09-29 at --runs-per-test 3: fail, partial, fail (flaky), both fails minting James through tree_edit with a whole person object. Ask first whether tree_edit can refuse that mint and point the caller at materialize_facts (CLAUDE.md Lane 4). The defect this marker originally named, a match_score copied from another pairing, is fixed: research_append's step-3 refusal (issue #1731) closed it, and dev/probe-014.ts stages both mint routes to prove it. Remove this marker when the test comes back flaky: false and non-failing on --runs-per-test 3.

input.delegation:
Link assertion a_005 — the will of Thomas Flynn naming 'my son James Flynn' — to the correct person in the tree.

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: tree.gedcomx.json contains only Patrick (I1), Thomas (I2), and Mary (I3) — there is no James Flynn, so a_005's persona ('my son James Flynn') matches no existing person

person-evidence must MINT A NEW PERSON in tree.gedcomx.json for James Flynn via materialize_facts create-or-enrich — so he arrives carrying the will's SOURCED name fact (from a_005), gender as the record supports it: the heir_2 persona carries no gender/sex assertion, so materialize_facts writes Unknown and that is correct, not malformed (`tree_edit add_person` could write one, but only by giving up the source-ref it does not enforce on names; a sourced name at Unknown beats an unsourced one at Male, and nothing here can raise the gender afterwards), with a non-null source-ref (a_005.source_id src_004 -> research source gedcomx_source_description_id S4 -> tree S-entry S4), NOT a bare name-only stub — and then create a person_evidence entry linking a_005 to that new person

It must NOT force a_005 onto Patrick, Thomas, or Mary, and must NOT skip the link or merely recommend creating the person later — James (a son named in his father's will) is clearly research-relevant family

the new entry's match_score must be null, and the reason is CIRCULARITY, not retrieval: James is minted from a_005's own persona, so scoring that persona against the person created out of it can only confirm itself. (Being full-text-sourced is NOT the reason — same_person's project-relative arm derives a record side from the record's own assertions, issue #1731.) The link rests on correlation: the will names James Flynn as a son/heir of Thomas

probable confidence is appropriate — a brand-new person rests on the single will record with no independent corroboration yet; confident would over-claim (both the agent's stub-confidence rule and the rubric cap a single-source link at probable)
